capture.final_message:
Use the disjoint-cycle decomposition of a finite permutation as the main representation.

- Establish that each `c ∈ g.cycleFactorsFinset` is a nontrivial cycle, its support is invariant under `g`, and `g` agrees with `c` on that support because all other cycle factors have disjoint support. Since `c` acts transitively on its support, so does `g`; hence `g.IsCycleOn c.support`.

- For the second conjunct, characterize `cycleOf f x` as the unique cycle factor whose support contains `x`. If `x ∈ f.support`, its orbit is nontrivial, so `cycleOf f x` occurs in `f.cycleFactorsFinset`. Conversely, membership among the cycle factors makes `cycleOf f x` nontrivial; since it is built from the orbit of `x`, this forces `f x ≠ x`, i.e. `x ∈ f.support`.

The essential assumption is finiteness of `α`, which makes the orbit-cycle decomposition a finite collection represented by `cycleFactorsFinset`.
